All endpoints operate on servers you have already added to a project in the
hosted inspector. Managing API keys remai

ns UI-only; see
[Not in the API yet](#not-in-the-api-yet).

## Base URL

```text theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
https:/

/app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```

The API is path-versioned. All routes on this page are relative to the base
URL above.

## Authe
curl -X POST \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Beare

r $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{}'
```

### Creating a key

1. Open [**Settings →
API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)\n in the hosted app (the card at the top of this page takes you there\n
directly).\n2. Click **Create API key**, name it, and pick the **organization** it will act in.\n3. Copy the key (`sk_…`) immediat

ely; **it is shown exactly once** and never
 stored by MCPJam in retrievable form.

Keys can be revoked from the same page at

any time. Revocation takes effect
immediately.

### Scope

A key is bound to one MCPJam organization at creation and acts **
as you,\ninside that organization**. Per-request authorization still applies: a call\nonly succeeds if the key's owner can access

that project and server. A key
can never reach projects outside its organization.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two deliberate restrictions

while in preview:
>
> * **API keys cannot manage API keys.** Requests to the key-management surface
> with an `sk_…` bearer f
ail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and revoke keys in\n> the UI.\n> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API.** Sign in to create key

s.

### Keep keys secret

Treat an API key like a password:

* Load it from an environment variable or secret manager; never
commit it to\n source control or ship it in client-side code.\n* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integration, named so you can
tell them apart.\n* Rotate by creating a replacement key, switching traffic, then revoking the old one.\n* If a key leaks, revoke

it immediately in
 [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

If you see `401 UNAUTHORIZED` with `d
etails.reason: \"ORPHANED_KEY\"`, the key\nis no longer bound to an organization and cannot be used; create a new key\nfrom [Setti

ngs](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

## Conventions

**Requests.** Operations on servers are `POST` with a JSON bo
dy (most accept\nan empty `{}`). **Reads**, the catalog listings and eval-run polling, are\n`GET` and take their options (`cursor`

, `limit`, filters) as query
parameters.

**Responses.** Three envelope shapes, used consistently:

| Kind | Shape |
| - | -
|\n| Single resource | The resource object directly |\n| Collection | `{ \"items\": [...], \"nextCursor\": \"...\" }`; `nextCurso
r` omitted on the last page |\n| Error | `{ \"code\": \"...\", \"message\": \"...\", \"details\": {...} }` with a matching HTTP st

atus |

**Pagination.** Collections are cursor-based. Pass the previous response's
`nextCursor` as `cursor` in the next request

(body field on `POST` lists,
query parameter on `GET` lists). Cursors are opaque; don't parse them.

**Authoring vs running su
ites.** `POST /eval-suites` creates a runnable suite\n(the suite plus its test cases) **synchronously** and responds `201` with th
e\n`suiteId`, WITHOUT running anything; author once, run later. `POST /eval-runs`\nis the async counterpart: it validates and crea
tes a run synchronously, then\ndetaches execution and responds `202` with a `runId`. Poll\n`GET /eval-runs/{runId}` until `status`

is `completed`, `failed`,
`cancelled`, or `timed_out`.

**IDs.** Every identifier the API takes is discoverable through the AP
I\nitself: `GET /projects` lists your projects, `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers`\nlists each project's servers, and `GET /proje

cts/{projectId}/eval-suites`
lists its eval suites. Start from `GET /me` to confirm which account a key
acts as.

## Errors
\
nErrors always use the canonical body `{ code, message, details? }`. The `code`\nis stable and machine-readable; `message` is huma

n-readable and may change;
`details` is an optional, unstructured bag.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `UNAUTHORIZ
ED` | 401 | Missing, invalid, revoked, or orphaned key |\n| `OAUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | The **target MCP server** needs an OAuth gran
t; distinct from a bad key |\n| `AUTH_REQUIRED` | 403 | The **target MCP server** allowed the connection and asked for sign-in on
this call. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge. Your key is fine; see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-challenges) |
\n| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Key is valid but not allowed to do this, or the **target MCP server** rejected the credentials MCPJam pres
ented (retrying with a different MCPJam key will not help; reconnect or re-authorize the server) |\n| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | M
alformed body or parameters |\n| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown project, server, or resource |\n| `CONFLICT` | 409 | The resource isn
't in a state that accepts this write, such as a stale `expectedRevision`, a duplicate name, or an environment that can't currentl
y be launched. Re-read and retry |\n| `FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` | 422 | The target server doesn't support this MCP capability |\n| `
RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests; see [Rate limits](#rate-limits) |\n| `SERVER_UNREACHABLE` | 502 | Could not connect to th
e target MCP server |\n| `TIMEOUT` | 504 | The target MCP server connected but didn't respond in time |\n| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500

| Something failed on our side |

New error codes may be **added** over time; treat unknown codes as
non-retryable failures unl
